speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते ।
सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथात्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥
iast:
yathā sarvagataṃ saukṣmyādākāśaṃ nopalipyate |
sarvatrāvasthito dehe tathātmā nopalipyate ||
english: As all-pervading space, being subtle, is not stained, so the self, present everywhere in the body, is not stained.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः ।
क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत ॥
iast:
yathā prakāśayatyekaḥ kṛtsnaṃ lokamimaṃ raviḥ |
kṣetraṃ kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnaṃ prakāśayati bhārata ||
english: As the one sun lights up this whole world, so the owner of the field lights up the whole field, Arjuna.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा ।
भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम् ॥
iast:
kṣetrakṣetrajñayorevamantaraṃ jñānacakṣuṣā |
bhūtaprakṛtimokṣaṃ ca ye viduryānti te param ||
english: Those who see with the eye of knowledge the difference between the field and its knower, and the way to freedom from the nature of beings, go to the supreme.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
परं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् ।
यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः ॥
iast:
paraṃ bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi jñānānāṃ jñānamuttamam |
yajjñātvā munayaḥ sarve parāṃ siddhimito gatāḥ ||
english: Again I will teach you the supreme knowledge, the highest of all knowledge, knowing which all the sages have gone from here to the highest perfection.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः ।
सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च ॥
iast:
idaṃ jñānamupāśritya mama sādharmyamāgatāḥ |
sarge'pi nopajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca ||
english: Taking refuge in this knowledge, people come to share my nature; they are not born even at creation, nor are they troubled at the dissolution.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन्गर्भं दधाम्यहम् ।
संभवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत ॥
iast:
mama yonirmahadbrahma tasmingarbhaṃ dadhāmyaham |
saṃbhavaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tato bhavati bhārata ||
english: Great Brahman is my womb; in it I place the seed, and from it all beings come into being, Arjuna.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः संभवन्ति याः ।
तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता ॥
iast:
sarvayoniṣu kaunteya mūrtayaḥ saṃbhavanti yāḥ |
tāsāṃ brahma mahadyonirahaṃ bījapradaḥ pitā ||
english: Whatever forms are born in any womb, son of Kunti, great Brahman is their womb, and I am the father who gives the seed.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः ।
निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम् ॥
iast:
sattvaṃ rajastama iti guṇāḥ prakṛtisaṃbhavāḥ |
nibadhnanti mahābāho dehe dehinamavyayam ||
english: Sattva, rajas and tamas, the gunas born of nature, bind the imperishable embodied one to the body, mighty-armed one.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम् ।
सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ ॥
iast:
tatra sattvaṃ nirmalatvātprakāśakamanāmayam |
sukhasaṅgena badhnāti jñānasaṅgena cānagha ||
english: Of these, sattva, being pure, is illuminating and free of affliction; it binds, sinless one, through attachment to happiness and attachment to knowledge.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् ।
तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् ॥
iast:
rajo rāgātmakaṃ viddhi tṛṣṇāsaṅgasamudbhavam |
tannibadhnāti kaunteya karmasaṅgena dehinam ||
english: Know rajas to be passion, springing from craving and attachment; it binds the embodied one, son of Kunti, through attachment to action.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् ।
प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत ॥
iast:
tamastvajñānajaṃ viddhi mohanaṃ sarvadehinām |
pramādālasyanidrābhistannibadhnāti bhārata ||
english: But know tamas to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings; it binds, Arjuna, through carelessness, laziness and sleep.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सत्त्वं सुखे संजयति रजः कर्मणि भारत ।
ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे संजयत्युत ॥
iast:
sattvaṃ sukhe saṃjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata |
jñānamāvṛtya tu tamaḥ pramāde saṃjayatyuta ||
english: Sattva attaches one to happiness, rajas to action, Arjuna; but tamas, veiling knowledge, attaches one to carelessness.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत ।
रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा ॥
iast:
rajastamaścābhibhūya sattvaṃ bhavati bhārata |
rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamaścaiva tamaḥ sattvaṃ rajastathā ||
english: Sattva rises by overpowering rajas and tamas, Arjuna; rajas, by overpowering sattva and tamas; and tamas likewise, by overpowering sattva and rajas.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते ।
ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत ॥
iast:
sarvadvāreṣu dehe'sminprakāśa upajāyate |
jñānaṃ yadā tadā vidyādvivṛddhaṃ sattvamityuta ||
english: When the light of knowledge shines through every gate of this body, then know that sattva is dominant.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा ।
रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥
iast:
lobhaḥ pravṛttirārambhaḥ karmaṇāmaśamaḥ spṛhā |
rajasyetāni jāyante vivṛddhe bharatarṣabha ||
english: Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness and longing: these arise when rajas is dominant, best of the Bharatas.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च ।
तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन ॥
iast:
aprakāśo'pravṛttiśca pramādo moha eva ca |
tamasyetāni jāyante vivṛddhe kurunandana ||
english: Darkness, inertia, carelessness and delusion: these arise when tamas is dominant, joy of the Kurus.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् ।
तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते ॥
iast:
yadā sattve pravṛddhe tu pralayaṃ yāti dehabhṛt |
tadottamavidāṃ lokānamalānpratipadyate ||
english: If the embodied one meets death when sattva is dominant, they reach the pure worlds of those who know the highest.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते ।
तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते ॥
iast:
rajasi pralayaṃ gatvā karmasaṅgiṣu jāyate |
tathā pralīnastamasi mūḍhayoniṣu jāyate ||
english: Meeting death in rajas, one is born among those attached to action; dying in tamas, one is born in deluded wombs.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम् ।
रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम् ॥
iast:
karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasyāhuḥ sāttvikaṃ nirmalaṃ phalam |
rajasastu phalaṃ duḥkhamajñānaṃ tamasaḥ phalam ||
english: The fruit of good action is said to be sattvic and pure; the fruit of rajas is pain, and the fruit of tamas is ignorance.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सत्त्वात्संजायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च ।
प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ॥
iast:
sattvātsaṃjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca |
pramādamohau tamaso bhavato'jñānameva ca ||
english: From sattva arises knowledge; from rajas, greed; from tamas come carelessness, delusion and ignorance.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः ।
जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः ॥
iast:
ūrdhvaṃ gacchanti sattvasthā madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ |
jaghanyaguṇavṛttisthā adho gacchanti tāmasāḥ ||
english: Those grounded in sattva rise upward; the rajasic stay in the middle; and the tamasic, living by the lowest guna, go downward.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति ।
गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति ॥
iast:
nānyaṃ guṇebhyaḥ kartāraṃ yadā draṣṭānupaśyati |
guṇebhyaśca paraṃ vetti madbhāvaṃ so'dhigacchati ||
english: When the seer sees no doer other than the gunas, and knows what is beyond the gunas, they come to my state of being.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन्देही देहसमुद्भवान् ।
जन्ममृत्युजरादुःखैर्विमुक्तोऽमृतमश्नुते ॥
iast:
guṇānetānatītya trīndehī dehasamudbhavān |
janmamṛtyujarāduḥkhairvimukto'mṛtamaśnute ||
english: Going beyond these three gunas, from which the body arises, the embodied one is freed from birth, death, old age and sorrow, and attains immortality.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
कैर्लिङ्गैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो ।
किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते ॥
iast:
kairliṅgaistrīnguṇānetānatīto bhavati prabho |
kimācāraḥ kathaṃ caitāṃstrīnguṇānativartate ||
english: Lord, by what signs is one known who has gone beyond these three gunas? How do they behave, and how do they go beyond the three gunas?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
प्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव ।
न द्वेष्टि संप्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति ॥
iast:
prakāśaṃ ca pravṛttiṃ ca mohameva ca pāṇḍava |
na dveṣṭi saṃpravṛttāni na nivṛttāni kāṅkṣati ||
english: One who does not resent light, activity or delusion when they arise, son of Pandu, nor long for them when they cease,

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते ।
गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते ॥
iast:
udāsīnavadāsīno guṇairyo na vicālyate |
guṇā vartanta ityeva yo'vatiṣṭhati neṅgate ||
english: who sits as if indifferent, unshaken by the gunas, who stays firm and does not waver, knowing that it is only the gunas at work,

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ।
तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः ॥
iast:
samaduḥkhasukhaḥ svasthaḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ |
tulyapriyāpriyo dhīrastulyanindātmasaṃstutiḥ ||
english: who is the same in pain and pleasure, rests in the self, regards a lump of earth, a stone and gold alike, is the same towards the pleasant and the unpleasant, steady, and the same in blame and praise,

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः ।
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते ॥
iast:
mānāpamānayostulyastulyo mitrāripakṣayoḥ |
sarvārambhaparityāgī guṇātītaḥ sa ucyate ||
english: the same in honour and dishonour, the same towards friend and foe, having given up all self-centred undertakings: such a person is said to have gone beyond the gunas.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते ।
स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान्ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
iast:
māṃ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate |
sa guṇānsamatītyaitānbrahmabhūyāya kalpate ||
english: One who serves me with unswerving devotion goes beyond these gunas and becomes fit to become Brahman.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च ।
शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च ॥
iast:
brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāhamamṛtasyāvyayasya ca |
śāśvatasya ca dharmasya sukhasyaikāntikasya ca ||
english: For I am the foundation of Brahman, of the immortal and imperishable, of eternal dharma, and of absolute happiness.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम् ।
छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् ॥
iast:
ūrdhvamūlamadhaḥśākhamaśvatthaṃ prāhuravyayam |
chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni yastaṃ veda sa vedavit ||
english: They speak of an imperishable fig tree with its roots above and its branches below, whose leaves are the Vedic hymns; whoever knows it knows the Veda.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा ।
गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः ।
अधश्च मूलान्यनुसंततानि ।
कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके ॥
iast:
adhaścordhvaṃ prasṛtāstasya śākhā |
guṇapravṛddhā viṣayapravālāḥ |
adhaśca mūlānyanusaṃtatāni |
karmānubandhīni manuṣyaloke ||
english: Its branches spread below and above, nourished by the gunas, with sense objects as their shoots; and below, its roots stretch out, binding to action in the human world.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते ।
नान्तो न चादिर्न च संप्रतिष्ठा ।
अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूल- ।
मसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा ॥
iast:
na rūpamasyeha tathopalabhyate |
nānto na cādirna ca saṃpratiṣṭhā |
aśvatthamenaṃ suvirūḍhamūla- |
masaṅgaśastreṇa dṛḍhena chittvā ||
english: Its form is not perceived here as it really is: neither its end, nor its beginning, nor its foundation. Having cut down this firmly rooted fig tree with the strong axe of non-attachment,

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्यं ।
यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः ।
तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये ।
यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी ॥
iast:
tataḥ padaṃ tatparimārgitavyaṃ |
yasmingatā na nivartanti bhūyaḥ |
tameva cādyaṃ puruṣaṃ prapadye |
yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā purāṇī ||
english: one should then seek that state from which those who reach it never return, thinking: "I take refuge in that primal Person from whom this ancient activity has flowed forth."

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा ।
अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः ।
द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै- ।
र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ॥
iast:
nirmānamohā jitasaṅgadoṣā |
adhyātmanityā vinivṛttakāmāḥ |
dvandvairvimuktāḥ sukhaduḥkhasaṃjñai- |
rgacchantyamūḍhāḥ padamavyayaṃ tat ||
english: Free of pride and delusion, having overcome the fault of attachment, always intent on the self, with desires turned away, freed from the pairs of opposites known as pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach that imperishable state.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः ।
यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
iast:
na tadbhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅko na pāvakaḥ |
yadgatvā na nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama ||
english: Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor fire lights it up; having gone there, people do not return. That is my supreme abode.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः ।
मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ॥
iast:
mamaivāṃśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ |
manaḥṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛtisthāni karṣati ||
english: An eternal part of me, becoming a living being in the world of the living, draws to itself the senses, with the mind as the sixth, which rest in nature.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः ।
गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात् ॥
iast:
śarīraṃ yadavāpnoti yaccāpyutkrāmatīśvaraḥ |
gṛhītvaitāni saṃyāti vāyurgandhānivāśayāt ||
english: When the lord of the body takes on a body and when it leaves one, it takes these with it and goes, as the wind carries scents from their source.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च ।
अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते ॥
iast:
śrotraṃ cakṣuḥ sparśanaṃ ca rasanaṃ ghrāṇameva ca |
adhiṣṭhāya manaścāyaṃ viṣayānupasevate ||
english: Presiding over hearing, sight, touch, taste and smell, and over the mind, it enjoys the objects of the senses.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् ।
विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः ॥
iast:
utkrāmantaṃ sthitaṃ vāpi bhuñjānaṃ vā guṇānvitam |
vimūḍhā nānupaśyanti paśyanti jñānacakṣuṣaḥ ||
english: Whether it is leaving the body, staying in it, or experiencing the world through the gunas, the deluded do not see it; those with the eye of knowledge see it.
